lessons.title: Select Columns DISTINCT
lessons.description: Select name and email from customers. Also write a query that uses DISTINCT to list the unique countries. The test checks that you get at least 3 rows.
learning_objectives: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn, and project only the columns you need instead of SELECT.
lessons.starter_code:
-- TODO: select each country only once (duplicate rows removed)
SELECT country FROM customers WHERE 0;

source.name: SQLite official documentation (sqlite.org) — SELECT with DISTINCT — 'duplicate rows are removed'

exercises.question: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn, and project only the columns you need instead of SELECT.
hints: Read the one job this step is practicing.
The example is about Selecting Columns DISTINCT.
SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers;
exercises.explanation: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn, and project only the columns you need instead of SELECT.

exercises.question: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn. For project only the columns you need instead of SELECT, which line lists each country once?
hints: Compare each line with the example.
One line matches the example.
SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers
exercises.explanation: DISTINCT keeps one row for each country.

exercises.question: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn. For project only the columns you need instead of SELECT, what value is displayed?
hints: Run the example in your head from the top.
The last line is what gets displayed.
exercises.explanation: The Selecting Columns DISTINCT program displays that value.
exercises.starter_code: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers ORDER BY country;

exercises.question: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn. For project only the columns you need instead of SELECT, build the line that lists each country once.
hints: Start at the left of the example.
Keep the example order.
SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers
exercises.explanation: DISTINCT keeps one row for each country.

exercises.question: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn. For project only the columns you need instead of SELECT, fill the blank so the line lists each country once.
hints: The blank is the missing piece of the example.
The example uses that piece.
DISTINCT
exercises.explanation: DISTINCT keeps one row for each country.

exercises.question: Plaza clerks recount crates before dawn. For project only the columns you need instead of SELECT, which line does a different job than the example?
hints: The other lines match the example.
One line is the odd one.
Line 1
exercises.explanation: The query lists every row, so repeated countries stay.

exercises.explanation: The second Selecting Columns DISTINCT program displays that value.
